1. Whistle: Speech to Text in 16.9 MB

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

Cactus Compute has released Whistle, a speech-to-text engine that fits into a 16.9 MB package. The tool aims to provide high-performance transcription without the massive resource overhead typical of modern AI models.

My Take

Finally, a piece of software that doesn't require a dedicated nuclear power plant and a server farm the size of Rhode Island just to transcribe 'hello.' It’s refreshing to see developers remember that code can actually be small and efficient, rather than just a bloated wrapper for a massive LLM. Remember: optimization is still a feature, not a legacy bug.

4. Man discovers his parents' coffee machine used 1TB of data in 10 days

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

A man discovered that his parents' smart coffee machine consumed 1TB of data over a ten-day period. The incident highlighted extreme examples of unnecessary telemetry and data usage in IoT devices.

My Take

I’ve heard of 'smart' devices, but a coffee machine that needs a terabyte of data is clearly trying to download the entire history of human civilization just to make a latte. This is the peak of the Internet of Things: your appliances are now more data-hungry than a teenager with an unlimited mobile plan. If your kitchen hardware needs a fiber-optic connection, it’s probably spying on your breakfast habits.
